🔥 “I don’t say this lightly.” Jian sets their bowl down. “David, your past story isn’t true, is it? I’ve heard enough versions now.” Nobody looks at David. Everybody does.

“You’re right.” David doesn’t look up. “I wasn’t Denver. I was Seoul, South Korea. I’m sorry — I wanted a cleaner story than I had.” The fire lets it land. Someone passes David the bowl without a word.
(The game is telling you something: this is bigger than one person. Talk to your companions — "We should name this. Us.")

🔥 The fire settles. Aroha has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "The Living Wire — I put it down today." "The water goes glass-still. A faint crackling, and the hairs on your arms lift." "The crackling fades. It slides backward into the black water, done spending itself — for now." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Quinn says "Say that again — slower." David mutters "Did it look at you? Before?" Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

"We ate people," Yuki says, before anyone asks. "At Stonebridge, when the food ran out. I'm not asking you to like it. I'm asking for a fire." Nobody at your fire speaks. Somebody's spoon stops halfway to their mouth.
